newsitem.title: USA: PECO Limerick, Pa. nuke seen on line Thurs.
newsitem.headline: PECO Limerick, Pa. nuke seen on line Thurs.

text.p: PECO Energy Co's 1,055 megawatt Limerick nuclear power unit 2 is expected to resume electricity production late Thursday following a scheduled maintenance shutdown, a company spokesman said.
"Late today it should synchronize to the (power) grid," spokesman Michael Wood said Thursday.
The unit, located in Montgomery County, Pa., was taken off line Jan 30 for scheduled maintenance and refueling.
"We are really preparing the unit for a long run," before its next maintenance and refueling outage, the spokesman said.

Limerick 2 was producing at five percent power, but had not resynchronized to the power grid and was "holding for dry well inspection," the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said in its daily plant status report for Thursday.
The adjoining 1,055 megawatt Limerick nuclear power unit 1 was operating at full capacity as of early Thursday, the NRC said.
